problems.title: Latency and throughput
problems.statement: A pipeline has 6 stages of 2 ns each and accepts a new item every 2 ns.

parts.prompt: Latency of one item, in ns?

problems.solution: Latency 12 ns; throughput one per 2 ns; 1,000 items take 12 + 999 × 2 = 2,010 ns. Throughput, not latency, dominates large jobs.

problems.title: Little's law on a new GPU
problems.statement: A GPU has 900 GB/s of DRAM bandwidth and 500 ns of memory latency. Each warp keeps 2 requests of 128 bytes in flight.

parts.prompt: Bytes in flight needed for full bandwidth?
If the GPU has 108 SMs, warps per SM needed?

problems.solution: 450,000 bytes; /256 = 1,758 warps; 16.3 per SM, well inside 64: this GPU can saturate memory at about 25% occupancy with 2 loads per warp.

problems.title: Warps and lanes
problems.solution: t = 7 + 3·32 + 1·128 = 231: warp 7, lane 7. With x = 32, every warp is one row.

problems.title: Divergence cost
problems.statement: A warp runs if (lane % 4 == 0) { A } else if (lane % 2 == 0) { B } else { C } then D. Costs: A 6, B 2, C 3, D 5 instructions; each test costs 1 instruction for the lanes that reach it.

parts.prompt: Instructions issued by the warp (tests included)?
SIMD efficiency, counting only A–D as useful, in %?

problems.solution: Issue slots: first test (1), A (6), second test (1, reached by 24 lanes), B (2), C (3), D (5): 18. Useful lane-slots: A runs on the 8 lanes with lane % 4 == 0 (48), B on the 8 lanes ≡ 2 mod 4 (16), C on the 16 odd lanes (48), D on all 32 (160): 272 of 576, 47.2%.

problems.title: Roofline
problems.statement: GPU: 20 TFLOP/s FP32, 1 TB/s. Kernel: 3 FLOPs per element, reads two FP32 arrays, writes one.

problems.title: Sectors
problems.statement: A warp reads 4-byte floats; lane ℓ reads element $3\ell + 8$ of an aligned array.
problems.solution: Bytes 32 + 12ℓ for ℓ = 0..31: 32 to 404, sectors 1 through 12: 12 sectors, 33.3%.

problems.title: Bank conflicts

parts.prompt: Smallest padded stride ≥ 24 that is conflict-free?

problems.solution: gcd(24, 32) = 8 passes. Any odd stride is conflict-free: 25.

problems.title: Occupancy
problems.statement: GW-1 rules (64 warps, 16 blocks, 65,536 registers in 256-register chunks per warp, 64 KB shared in 256-byte chunks). 128-thread blocks, 48 registers, 12 KB shared memory.
problems.solution: Warps allow 16 blocks; registers: 1,536 per warp → 42 warps → 10 blocks; shared: 64/12 = 5 blocks. Shared memory binds: 5 blocks, 20 warps (31.25%).

problems.title: Reduction
problems.statement: A 512-thread block reduces with sequential addressing in shared memory down to 32 values, then one warp finishes with shuffles.

parts.prompt: Shared-memory rounds (with a barrier each) before the warp step?

problems.solution: 512 → 256 → 128 → 64 → 32: 4 rounds; then 5 shuffle steps for 32 values.

problems.title: Histogram contention
problems.statement: A warp's 32 lanes hold values 0, 0, …, 0 (20 lanes), 5 (6 lanes), 9 (6 lanes).
problems.solution: 20 lanes on one bin: 20 serialised updates. Aggregated: one per distinct value, 3.

problems.title: Memory ordering
problems.statement: Block A writes data then a flag; block B polls the flag then reads data.

options: A device-scope fence (or release) between A's two writes

problems.solution: Release on the producer, acquire on the consumer. __syncthreads only orders within a block; a grid barrier isn't needed (and isn't available in ordinary launches).

problems.title: GEMM bounds
problems.statement: Square FP32 GEMM, n = 2048, on the GPU from Problem 5 (20 TFLOP/s, 1 TB/s).

parts.prompt: Time at peak compute, in ms?
Best-case DRAM time (A, B read once, C written once), in ms?
DRAM time with 32 × 32 shared tiles and no L2 reuse (A, B read n/32 times), in ms?

problems.solution: (a) 0.859 ms. (b) 0.050 ms. (c) 2.164 ms: about 2.5× the compute time, so 32 × 32 tiles leave the kernel memory-bound; bigger tiles (or L2 reuse between blocks) are needed.

problems.title: Register tiling
problems.statement: A thread computes a 4 × 8 tile of C.

problems.title: Pipelining
problems.statement: Each K-step's math takes 150 cycles; a tile load takes 700 cycles of latency.

problems.title: Tensor cores and precision
problems.statement: FP16 inputs with entries $k/32$ for integers $|k| \le 32$, FP32 accumulation, K = 4096.

parts.prompt: Are all products exact in FP32?
Are all partial sums exact in FP32?
options: Yes: they're multiples of 2⁻¹⁰ below 2¹², needing at most 22 bits

problems.solution: Products are multiples of $2^{-10}$ with magnitude ≤ 1; sums are multiples of $2^{-10}$ with magnitude ≤ 4096 = $2^{12}$: at most 22 significant bits, inside FP32's 24. Every summation order gives the same, exact result, so a test can demand bit equality.

problems.title: Choose the fix
problems.statement: Match each symptom to the first fix.

parts.prompt: Stride-32 global reads in a transpose
Tiled GEMM stuck at a third of peak, issue-bound

problems.solution: Staging, padding, register tiling: each fix follows from the specific bottleneck.
